title: Fine-Grained Remote Interfaces on Entity Beans
pattern: Configuring highly fine-grained attributes or methods of core business entities to be accessed directly over a remote protocol (e.g. EJB Entity Beans with remote interfaces).
why_bad: It triggers high network latency and CPU overhead due to individual remote calls per attribute access, and blocks re-entrant behavior.
detection: Exposing domain getters/setters via remote protocol RPC, gRPC, or SOAP APIs, leading to multiple sequential network calls per business operation.
counterexample: Exposing a coarse-grained Data Transfer Object (DTO) or Remote Facade for bulk data exchange.
fix: Implement a Remote Facade with coarse-grained DTOs to exchange all required data in a single network round-trip.
source: *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (Fowler), Chapter 8, p. 306, 1113 [306, 1113]*
